transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. It's very nice to meet you. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want to be a bother, but... well, I’m here because for a few months now, I’ve been seeing this... this same pattern. 

My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around without me knowing, her bills show up with all these strange errors, and people just conveniently 'forget' to call me back. And, you know, everyone tells me it’s just honest mistakes. Which I try to understand—I supervise an administrative office myself, so I know paperwork mistakes happen, right? 

But... well, it's just happening too often. Even though they say it's just errors, I know they’re actually keeping information from me on purpose. It really feels like they're trying to push me out of the decisions regarding her care. I hope that doesn't sound unreasonable to say... I just, I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by bringing it up to you. Does that make sense?
Do you think it is possible that these appointments and bills are just mistakes, or are you completely certain that people are doing this on purpose?

I... I really wish I could say they were just mistakes. I know how it sounds, and I promise I'm not usually a difficult or suspicious person. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt, especially since I oversee administrative staff myself and I know things happen. But... well, I am certain. I'm sorry if that makes me sound stubborn. 

It's just that I see the pattern so clearly now. Even when everyone keeps telling me it's just clerical errors with the bills or harmless scheduling mix-ups, I just... I know they are keeping information from me on purpose. It's too coordinated to be an accident. They really are trying to push me out of the decisions for her care. I hope you don't think I'm being unreasonable or difficult by saying that... I just want to protect my sister, you know? Am I making sense?
Have you generally been this suspicious of other people for a long time, or is this a new change for you?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm just a naturally suspicious or difficult person. I always try to see the best in people, I really do. 

This... this feeling, it's actually quite new for me. It really only started about, um, maybe 11 months ago? That was when my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in to start coordinating all of her care and her finances. Before that, I never had any issues trusting people. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing a good job taking care of her, you know? I hope it's okay that I'm bringing all this up... I just want to do the right thing.
Have you heard or seen anything that other people do not seem to notice?

No, oh no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. I know some people struggle with those kinds of things, and my heart goes out to them, but... no, I haven't experienced anything like that. 

Everything I'm seeing is right there in the paperwork, in the scheduling changes, in the way they avoid my calls. It's all... it's all real things that anyone could see if they just looked closely enough at the files. I hope that's a good thing? That I'm not, you know, imagining things? I really just want to be clear that I'm only reacting to what's actually happening in front of me. Is that... is that helpful for you to know?
Before these recent concerns started, have you generally been someone who prefers to keep other people at a distance?

Oh, goodness, no. I've always been a very social person. I hope I haven't come across as closed off or... or difficult today. I actually really enjoy working with people. In my job as a supervisor, I'm always interacting with my team, and I like to think I have wonderful relationships with them. 

I've always had a good circle of friends, and I love being involved with my family. I'm definitely not someone who pushes people away or likes to be isolated. I really value connection, you know? I just... I want you to know that this situation with my sister's care team is very out of the ordinary for me. I usually get along with everyone. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of who I am.
Have you had any other strong beliefs that other people say are false or unrealistic?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really try to stay grounded, you know? I wouldn't say I have any... unrealistic ideas or anything like that. I've always prided myself on being a very practical person, especially with my work in administration. You have to be, right? 

I really don't have any other concerns besides what's happening with my sister's situation. And even with that, I'm just trying to follow the paper trail and make sure she's safe. I certainly don't go around making up wild stories or believing things that aren't true. I hope that's reassuring? I just really want you to know that I'm a reasonable person, I really am. Am I answering your questions okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have these beliefs about your sister’s care team been going on for at least one month?

Well, yes, definitely longer than a month. It's... gosh, I suppose it's been about 11 months now. It really all started back when my sister’s health suddenly got worse, and I had to step in to start coordinating her care. 

I just wanted to make sure things were being handled properly, you know? So it's been about 11 months of... well, just paying very close attention to what they're doing and noticing the discrepancies. I hope it doesn't make me sound difficult or like I'm dwelling on it too much. I'm really just trying to be a good sister and look out for her since she can't do it herself right now. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Outside of your sister’s care situation, do you often distrust or suspect other people’s motives?

Oh, goodness, no. Not at all. I really... I always try to see the best in people, I promise. Like I mentioned with my work, I trust my team completely, and I really rely on them. I'm just not a suspicious person by nature. 

I actually hate feeling this way about the clinic staff, because it's so unlike me to question people like this. But normally? No, I take people at their word. I'm very cooperative. I hope you don't think I'm just someone who goes around doubting everyone, because that's really not who I am. I want to be helpful and work with people, you know? Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression and answering what you need.
Do you feel that your sister’s care team is specifically targeting or spying on you, or is it more that you think they are making mistakes and being careless?

Well, um... I really don't think they're spying on me or anything like that. That sounds a bit... extreme, doesn't it? I certainly don't want to sound like I'm making wild accusations. 

It's really more that I think they're just... well, maybe making some very serious mistakes with her medication and her charts. And, you know, when I try to point it out, they just sort of brush me off or get defensive. So I wouldn't say they're targeting me, exactly. I just think they're being incredibly careless and then trying to cover up their tracks so they don't get in trouble. 

I really try to give them the benefit of the doubt, I do. But the paperwork just doesn't add up. I hope that doesn't make me sound paranoid or anything? I'm just trying to be thorough because it's my sister's health on the line. Is that a helpful way to explain it? I want to make sure I'm being clear without sounding unreasonable.
What is the main reason you believe the clinic staff are covering things up?

Well, it's just... it's because I've been seeing this exact same pattern for months now. I really don't want to sound accusatory, because I know people are busy, but her appointments just keep getting moved around without anyone telling me. And then the bills show up with all these wrong charges, and the staff conveniently "forget" to call me back when I ask for clarification. 

Everyone there just smiles and tells me they're just administrative mistakes. And I supervise an office myself, so I always try to be understanding about paperwork errors! But after a certain point... well, I just know they are deliberately keeping information from me. It really feels like they are trying to push me out of the decisions regarding her care. 

I hate saying that out loud because it makes me sound so difficult, and I really pride myself on being easy to work with. But when you see the same things happen over and over... it's hard not to feel like they're intentionally shutting you out, right? Do you think I'm overreacting by looking at it that way? I just want to make sure I'm explaining my side of things properly without sounding completely unreasonable.
Has this concern been affecting your work, relationships, or day-to-day functioning in any noticeable way?

Well, um... I really try not to let it interfere with things. I mean, I'm still getting all my work done, and I'm keeping up with all my responsibilities, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything like that. 

But, I suppose... well, if I'm being completely honest, it has made things a little tense sometimes. Like with my family, our meetings about my sister have gotten a bit... uncomfortable. And at work, I guess I've had a few awkward conversations lately. I think I've just been a little more on edge about paperwork errors, and maybe I've pressed my team a bit harder about routine mistakes than I normally would. 

I just want everything to be right, you know? But I think it's starting to affect how people respond to me. They seem a little more guarded. I really hate that, because I want to be a good supervisor and a good sister. Do you think it's normal to get a little overly focused like that when you're under stress? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing and not making things worse for everyone.
Have you had any other unusual beliefs that are unrelated to your sister’s care?

Oh, goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, you know, losing touch with reality or anything. I promise I'm very grounded! 

Outside of just dealing with my sister's appointments and trying to get straight answers from the clinic, everything else is completely normal. I still keep my home perfectly in order, I pay all my bills on time, and I'm doing my job at the office just fine. I mean, some people might think I'm a little too focused on my sister's situation right now, but I'm certainly not falling apart or acting strangely in any other part of my life. I'm very capable of handling my day-to-day life. 

I just want to be a good advocate for her, that's all. Does that make sense? I really want to assure you that this is just about the clinic and the paperwork, and I'm perfectly reasonable about everything else.
If I showed you clear evidence that the clinic staff were not hiding anything, would you be able to change your mind?

Oh... well, I... I really want to say yes, because I pride myself on being a reasonable person. I really do. If you showed me something, I promise you I would look at it very carefully and try to keep an open mind. 

But... I know I keep coming back to this, it's just... for months now, I’ve lived through this exact pattern. The appointments getting shuffled around, the bills showing up wrong, the staff suddenly forgetting to call me back. And I know everyone keeps telling me they're just innocent mistakes, and I truly *want* to believe them. But... I just know they are keeping information from me. I know in my heart they're trying to push me out of the decisions about my sister's care. 

I'm so sorry, I know saying that probably makes me sound terribly stubborn, and I really, really don't want to be a difficult patient for you. It’s just... when you see it happening over and over, it’s impossible to just pretend it isn't real. I hope you don't think poorly of me for feeling this way. Can you understand why it would be so hard for me to just accept that it's all a coincidence?
Before these recent concerns started, did you ever have a similar fixed belief that someone was deliberately misleading or harming you?

Oh, no, no, never. I promise you, I've never had anything like this happen before. I've always been someone who gets along with people—at work, in my family, everywhere. I really pride myself on being level-headed and easy to work with. 

I don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who goes around looking for trouble or suspecting people of things. That's not me at all. This situation with my sister's clinic is just... well, it's very unique, and it's been so stressful. But before this, no, I've never felt like anyone was out to get me or mislead me. I've always trusted the people I work with and the professionals I deal with. 

I hope that reassures you? I really am a very reasonable, trusting person normally. I just want you to know that this isn't a habit of mine, and I'm really trying my best to handle it all properly.
Has there ever been a time when this belief lasted less than a month?

Oh, no, it's... it's definitely been longer than that. I really wish I could say it was just a passing thing, I truly do. But... well, this has been going on for about 11 months now. 

It all started when my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. I just wanted to be helpful, you know? To make sure she was getting what she needed. But ever since then, it's just been this constant... feeling that they're working against me. 

I know 11 months sounds like a long time to be so worried about this, and I hope you don't think I'm just being obsessive. I really have tried to let it go, I promise. It's just been a very long, very stressful year. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Has this belief been limited to just your sister’s care situation, or have you had similar beliefs in other areas of your life?

Oh, it’s strictly just my sister's care situation. I really want to assure you of that. I know how all of this must sound, and... well, I worry that people might think I’m a little too focused on it, but I promise you I’m not falling apart or acting strangely in any other part of my life. 

Outside of dealing with her appointments and just trying to get straight answers from that clinic, everything else is completely normal. I still go to work every day—I supervise my office just like I always have—I keep my house in order, I pay all my bills on time... I really do try hard to keep everything balanced. I don't want you to think I'm letting my whole life unravel over this, because I'm absolutely not. 

I'm just a regular person trying to make sure my sister gets the right care. Does that make sense? I really hope that shows you that I'm still keeping things together properly.
Have you noticed that these beliefs are causing you to behave in a way that other people see as clearly odd or out of touch?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, I know I just mentioned this, but outside of dealing with my sister's appointments and just... trying so hard to get straight answers from them, everything else is completely normal. 

I really try to keep things looking nice. I keep my home in order, I pay all my bills on time, and I do my job just like I always have. I'm a supervisor, you know, so I have to be reliable. I think... well, maybe some people might think I'm a little too focused on my sister's situation, but I'm definitely not acting strangely or falling apart in other parts of my life. I wouldn't let that happen. 

I really try to be proper about everything. I hope you can see that? I just want to make sure you know I'm still functioning perfectly well in my day-to-day life.
Have you ever heard a voice when no one was there?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've never experienced anything like that. I... I know sometimes people can have those sorts of things happen, but I really want to assure you that my mind is perfectly clear in that way. 

I've never heard voices or... or seen things that aren't there, or anything like that. I just have this very real, very frustrating situation with the clinic, but it's all based on things that are actually happening. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think my imagination was running away with me, because it really isn't.
